mainTopic: The order and units of the יום הכפורים blood sprinklings, who is atoned for, and what happens when the blood (or a מצורע's oil) spills
overview: This amud first closes an earlier point: the משנה simply is not talking about the קטורת. עולא then rules that slaughtering the שעיר before the פר's blood is sprinkled inside does not count. He explains that the משנה's case of 'just sprinkle again' refers only to the היכל sprinklings, and רבי אפס agrees. A ברייתא reads the verse 'וכפר את מקדש הקודש' as listing places and people atoned for. רבי יהודה says כהנים, ישראל, and לוים all get atonement from the שעיר המשתלח, while רבי שמעון says the כהנים get theirs from the פר. Another ברייתא teaches that the sprinklings in the לפני ולפנים, the היכל, and on the מזבח are each a separate כפרה. So if blood spills, a finished unit is never repeated. The unnamed חכמים (רבי מאיר) say an interrupted unit restarts, and רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say he continues where he stopped. רבי יוחנן explains that both sides read the word 'אחת' in one verse differently. The גמרא shows the same מחלוקת applies to the מצורע's לוג of oil, and explains from the double 'leftover' wording why the oil on the head is not essential. A new statement of רבי יוחנן begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The משנה is not discussing the incense
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects an earlier attempted proof. The proof was based on the משנה not mentioning the קטורת. The answer is that the משנה is simply not talking about the קטורת.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not speaking about the incense.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is closing off the previous discussion. It rejects a proof that was built on the משנה's silence about the קטורת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone tried to learn from the משנה that new קטורת is not needed after a new פר is slaughtered, because the משנה does not say so. The גמרא answers that the משנה only discusses the blood sprinklings. Its silence about the קטורת proves nothing, and in practice he does take new קטורת.

keyTerms.meaning: The incense offered in the קודש הקדשים on יום הכפורים
'It is not discussing' (that topic)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read this as 'no new קטורת is needed.' It means only that the משנה did not bother to mention the קטורת.

phrases.english: It is not speaking about the incense.
phrases.notes: The משנה is focused on the blood, so its silence about the incense proves nothing.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּקְטוֹרֶת לָא קָא מַיְירֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the discussion earlier.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof drawn from the משנה's silence about new קטורת
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה deals only with the blood sprinklings, so its silence about the קטורת proves nothing.

steps.title: עולא: slaughtering the goat too early is worthless
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that if the שעיר is slaughtered before the פר's blood is sprinkled, the slaughter does not count at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: A goat that he slaughtered before the sprinkling of the bull's blood — it is as if he did nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא states a new rule about the order of the יום הכפורים service. If the שעיר is slaughtered too early, the slaughter is invalid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The order is: the פר's blood is sprinkled inside first, and only then is the שעיר slaughtered. עולא says this order is essential, so the early slaughter is useless. That means a new שעיר would have to be slaughtered.

keyTerms.meaning: The goat offering (here, the goat for 'ה)
The כהן גדול's bull offering
The sprinkling (placement) of its blood
'He did nothing at all' — the act is invalid

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that on יום הכפורים the order of the service is not just a good idea. Doing things out of order can cancel an act.

phrases.english: Ulla said:

phrases.aramaic: שָׂעִיר שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ קוֹדֶם מַתַּן דָּמוֹ שֶׁל פַּר —
phrases.english: A goat that he slaughtered before the sprinkling of the bull's blood —
he has done nothing at all.
phrases.notes: The slaughter is invalid and must be done again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: שָׂעִיר שֶׁשְּׁחָטוֹ קוֹדֶם מַתַּן דָּמוֹ שֶׁל פַּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Slaughtering the שעיר before the פר's blood has been sprinkled is invalid.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה to עולא
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says that if the שעיר's blood came before the פר's blood, he only needs to sprinkle again. According to עולא, he should need to slaughter again.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: If he put the goat's blood before the bull's blood, he goes back and sprinkles from the goat's blood after the bull's blood. If עולא were right, it should have said he goes back and slaughters!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks עולא from a משנה. That משנה lets the original שעיר stay valid even when things were done out of order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שעיר's blood was sprinkled before the פר's blood, the שעיר must also have been slaughtered before the פר's blood was sprinkled. Yet the משנה only asks him to sprinkle again from the same שעיר's blood. This suggests the early slaughter was fine, which goes against עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We learned' (in a משנה)
He did it earlier (put it first)
He goes back and sprinkles again
'And if it were so' (if your claim were correct)
'It should have said'

phrases.aramaic: תְּנַן: הִקְדִּים דַּם הַשָּׂעִיר לְדַם הַפָּר —
phrases.english: We learned: If he put the goat's blood before the bull's blood —

phrases.aramaic: יַחְזוֹר וְיַזֶּה מִדַּם הַשָּׂעִיר אַחַר דַּם הַפָּר.
phrases.english: he goes back and sprinkles from the goat's blood after the bull's blood.
And if it were so (as Ulla says) —
it should have said he goes back and slaughters (a new goat)!

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּנַן: הִקְדִּים דַּם הַשָּׂעִיר לְדַם הַפָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's rule from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's rule that an early slaughter of the שעיר is invalid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה only requires sprinkling again, not slaughtering again. That implies the original slaughter stayed valid even though it was done out of order.

steps.title: עולא: the משנה means the Sanctuary sprinklings
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that the משנה is talking about the sprinklings in the היכל, not the sprinklings in the קודש הקדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא explained it as referring to the sprinklings in the Sanctuary.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the challenge. The mistake in the משנה happened during the היכל sprinklings, which come later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the time the היכל sprinklings happen, the פר's blood has already been sprinkled in the לפני ולפנים. So the שעיר was slaughtered at the right time, and only the היכל order got mixed up. Fixing that only requires sprinkling again, which fits with עולא's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained (interpreted) it
The blood sprinklings done in the היכל (on the curtain)

phrases.english: Ulla explained it as referring to the sprinklings in the Sanctuary.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּרְגְּמָא עוּלָּא, בְּמַתָּנוֹת שֶׁבַּהֵיכָל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case of the משנה (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה seemed to be about any sprinkling out of order, including the inner ones.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is only about the היכל sprinklings, after the inner ones were already done correctly. So the שעיר's slaughter was valid.

steps.title: רבי אפס says the same
steps.stepSummary: רבי אפס independently gives the same explanation of the משנה as עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so too Rabbi Afes said: it refers to the sprinklings in the Sanctuary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds that another אמורא, רבי אפס, says the same thing. This strengthens עולא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new idea is added here. A second authority agrees that the משנה is about the היכל sprinklings, which makes עולא's reading more convincing.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And likewise said' — another authority agrees
An early אמורא in ארץ ישראל

steps.whatToRemember: עולא: the inner sprinklings of the פר's blood must come before the שעיר is slaughtered. The משנה's case of 'just sprinkle again' is about the היכל stage only.

phrases.aramaic: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי אַפָּס, בְּמַתָּנוֹת שֶׁבַּהֵיכָל.
phrases.english: And so too Rabbi Afes said: it refers to the sprinklings in the Sanctuary.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן אָמַר רַבִּי אַפָּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 4.
steps.raayaObject: The reading that the משנה is about the היכל sprinklings

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: likewise in the Sanctuary and on the altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. If blood spills, the same rule applies in the היכל and at the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And likewise in the Sanctuary and likewise on the altar, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא quotes the משנה to begin a new discussion about the different places atoned for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the rule of starting a set of sprinklings over applies to each stage separately: the היכל and the golden מזבח. The quote opens the way for a ברייתא that lists the areas atoned for on יום הכפורים.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sanctuary, the room outside the קודש הקדשים
The altar (here, the golden inner altar)
'Etc.' — the quote continues in the משנה

phrases.english: 'And likewise in the Sanctuary and likewise on the altar, etc.'
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה introducing the next section.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֵן בַּהֵיכָל וְכֵן בַּמִּזְבֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule of restarting the sprinklings applies separately in the היכל and at the מזבח.

steps.title: The ברייתא: which places the verse atones for
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the verse to say that atonement is made for the לפני ולפנים, the היכל, the מזבח, and the courtyards.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'And he shall atone for the holy sanctuary' — this is the innermost room; 'the Tent of Meeting' — this is the Sanctuary; 'altar' — as it sounds; 'he shall atone' — these are the courtyards.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that goes through the verse phrase by phrase. It first matches each phrase to a place in the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each phrase of the verse is matched to a location. The second 'יכפר', which has no object of its own, is read as including the עזרות.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The Rabbis taught' — introduces a ברייתא
The innermost room, the קודש הקדשים
Just as it sounds (its plain meaning)
The courtyards of the מקדש

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
'And he shall atone for the holy sanctuary' —
this is the innermost room (Holy of Holies);
'the Tent of Meeting' — this is the Sanctuary;
'altar' — as it sounds;
'he shall atone' — these are the courtyards.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְכִפֶּר אֶת מִקְדַּשׁ הַקּוֹדֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא connected to the משנה quoted in step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verse covers atonement for the לפני ולפנים, the היכל, the מזבח, and the עזרות.

steps.title: The ברייתא: which people the verse atones for
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues and matches the rest of the verse to groups of people: כהנים, ישראל, and לוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'The priests' — as it sounds; 'the people of the assembly' — these are Israelites; 'he shall atone' — these are the Levites.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves from places to people. It matches each phrase of the verse to a group.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Again a third 'יכפר' with no clear object is used to add a group, this time the לוים. Now the verse covers all three groups of the Jewish people, which sets up the conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: Priests
'The people of the assembly' — read here as ישראל
Levites

phrases.english: 'the priests' — as it sounds;
'the people of the assembly' — these are the Israelites;
'he shall atone' — these are the Levites.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּהֲנִים כְּמַשְׁמָעָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The verse covers atonement for כהנים, ישראל, and לוים.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: all groups share one atonement through the scapegoat
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה concludes that since the verse lists everyone together, כהנים, ישראל, and לוים are all atoned for equally by the שעיר המשתלח for other sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were all made equal for one atonement: all of them are atoned for through the scapegoat for other sins. These are the words of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהודה draws the legal conclusion from the verse. All groups share the same atonement through the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the verse puts all the groups into one atonement, רבי יהודה learns that the שעיר המשתלח covers all of them equally. This is for 'other sins,' meaning sins that are not about טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. The words 'דברי רבי יהודה' signal that another תנא will disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: They were made equal
One (shared) atonement
The scapegoat sent away to עזאזל
Other sins (not involving טומאה of the מקדש)

steps.confusionAlert: 'Other sins' does not mean every sin. It excludes sins of טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. For those, the כהנים get atonement through the פר and ישראל through the inner שעיר.
steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, the שעיר המשתלח atones for כהנים, ישראל, and לוים all alike, for sins other than טומאת מקדש.
steps.whyThisMatters: 'דברי רבי יהודה' marks this as one side of a מחלוקת. The next part of the sugya will bring another view about whether the כהנים are included.

phrases.english: They were all made equal for one atonement,
meaning that all of them gain atonement through the scapegoat
for the other sins,
phrases.notes: Sins other than טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּשְׁווּ כּוּלָּן לְכַפָּרָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the legal rule from the readings in steps 7 and 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, כהנים, ישראל, and לוים are all atoned for equally by the שעיר המשתלח for other sins.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the bull's blood atones for the כהנים like the goat's blood atones for ישראל
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון compares the two inside offerings. The שעיר's blood atones for ישראל for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, and the פר's blood does the same for the כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: the blood of the goat that is brought inside atones for ישראל for the sin of טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. In the same way, the blood of the bull atones for the כהנים for that same sin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון begins his own view, which differs from רבי יהודה's. He starts by matching up the blood of the שעיר and the blood of the פר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees on this part. The פר is the כהנים' offering and the שעיר is ישראל's offering for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. רבי שמעון sets up this parallel so he can extend it to the confession in the next line.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as... so too. A formula for comparing two cases.
Entering the מקדש or eating קדשים while impure.
The blood of the כהן גדול's bull.
Whose service is done inside, in the קודש הקדשים.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
Just as the blood of the goat that is done inside
atones for Israel
for impurity of the Temple and its holy things,

phrases.aramaic: כָּךְ דַּם הַפָּר מְכַפֵּר עַל הַכֹּהֲנִים
phrases.english: so too the blood of the bull atones for the priests
for impurity of the Temple and its holy things.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁדַּם הַשָּׂעִיר הַנַּעֲשֶׂה בִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens רבי שמעון's opposing view to רבי יהודה's ruling in Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פר's blood atones for the כהנים for טומאת מקדש וקדשיו, just as the שעיר's blood does for ישראל.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: the bull's confession atones for the priests' other sins
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון finishes the parallel. Just as the confession over the שעיר המשתלח atones for ישראל's other sins, the confession over the פר atones for the כהנים' other sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: And just as the confession said over the שעיר המשתלח atones for ישראל for all other sins, the confession said over the bull atones for the כהנים for all other sins.
steps.whatsHappening: This is רבי שמעון's main point. The כהנים get atonement for their other sins through the פר's confession, not through the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה said the שעיר המשתלח atones for כהנים, ישראל, and לוים equally. רבי שמעון disagrees. He says the כהנים already have their own confession over the פר, so the שעיר המשתלח covers ישראל only.

keyTerms.meaning: Confession. The כהן גדול speaks it over the animal.
All other sins, besides טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.
The goat sent away to עזאזל.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: the שעיר המשתלח atones for everyone, כהנים included. רבי שמעון: the כהנים get atonement from their own פר, both its blood and its confession.

phrases.english: And just as the confession of the sent-away goat
atones for Israel for other sins,
so too the confession of the bull
atones for the priests for other sins.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֵׁם שֶׁוִּידּוּי שֶׁל שָׂעִיר הַמִּשְׁתַּלֵּחַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the parallel begun in Step 10 and reaches רבי שמעון's real disagreement with רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פר's confession atones for the כהנים' other sins, so they are not atoned for by the שעיר המשתלח.

steps.title: A ברייתא: each place of sprinkling is its own separate atonement
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the verse: הקודש means the לפני ולפנים, אהל מועד means the היכל, and מזבח means the altar. So each one is a separate כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: "And he finishes atoning for the קודש" refers to the לפני ולפנים. "אהל מועד" refers to the היכל. "מזבח" means just what it says. This teaches that each one is a separate atonement of its own.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that reads the verse closely. It sets up the practical rules that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse lists three places separately, so each set of sprinklings counts as its own unit of כפרה. This is the source for what happens when blood spills: only the unit that was in progress is affected.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught. Introduces a ברייתא.
The innermost room, the קודש הקדשים.
The Sanctuary, the room just outside the קודש הקדשים.
According to its plain meaning.
An atonement that stands on its own.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And he finishes atoning for the holy place"
this is the innermost sanctum;
"Tent of Meeting" — this is the Sanctuary;
"altar" — as it sounds;
this teaches that all of them
are each a separate atonement on their own.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: ״וְכִלָּה מִכַּפֵּר אֶת הַקּוֹדֶשׁ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of who is atoned for and returns to the rule about spilled blood from Step 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The sprinklings in the לפני ולפנים, the היכל, and on the מזבח are each a separate כפרה.

steps.title: Blood spilled in the middle of the inside sprinklings
steps.stepSummary: If the blood spills after only some of the inside sprinklings, the חכמים say to bring new blood and restart the inside sprinklings. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say he continues from where he stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: From here they said: if he did some of the sprinklings inside and then the blood spilled, he brings new blood and starts the inside sprinklings over. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say: he only starts from the place where he stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא applies the 'separate atonement' idea to a real case: blood spills partway through the inside sprinklings. Two opinions follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים treat each unit as one whole act, so an interrupted unit must be redone completely with new blood. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון hold that the sprinklings already done still count. The new blood only has to finish what is left.

keyTerms.meaning: From here they said. A rule is being drawn from the verse.
Sprinklings of blood. Literally, gifts.
And the blood spilled.
From the beginning.
From the place where he stopped.

steps.confusionAlert: Even for the חכמים, 'start from the beginning' means the beginning of the inside unit only, not the whole יום כפורים service.

phrases.english: From here they said:
If he gave some of the sprinklings inside
and the blood spilled,
he brings other blood
and begins from the start with the inside sprinklings.
Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say:
He begins only from the place where he stopped.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכָּאן אָמְרוּ: נָתַן מִקְצָת מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁבִּפְנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the 'separate atonement' reading from Step 12 to a practical case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: restart the interrupted inside unit with new blood. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון: continue from where he stopped.

steps.title: Blood spilled after finishing the inside sprinklings
steps.stepSummary: If he finished all the inside sprinklings and then the blood spilled, he brings new blood and begins with the היכל sprinklings. He does not repeat the inside.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he finished the inside sprinklings and then the blood spilled, he brings new blood and starts from the beginning of the sprinklings in the היכל.
steps.whatsHappening: A second case: the inside unit was already complete when the blood spilled. The finished unit stays done, and he moves on to the היכל with new blood.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because each place is its own כפרה, a completed unit is never undone. This case shows the 'separate atonement' idea most clearly, and no one disagrees with it.

keyTerms.meaning: He finished.
Other blood, from a newly slaughtered animal.
That are in the Sanctuary.

phrases.english: If he finished the sprinklings inside
and the blood spilled,
he brings other blood
and begins from the start with the Sanctuary sprinklings.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּמַר אֶת הַמַּתָּנוֹת שֶׁבִּפְנִים וְנִשְׁפַּךְ הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from an interrupted inside unit to a completed one.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A completed unit is not repeated. New blood begins the next unit, the היכל.

steps.title: Blood spilled in the middle of the Sanctuary sprinklings
steps.stepSummary: If the blood spills partway through the היכל sprinklings, the חכמים say to restart the היכל unit. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון again say he continues from where he stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did some of the sprinklings in the היכל and the blood spilled, he brings new blood and starts the היכל over. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say: he only starts from the place where he stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: The same dispute from Step 13 is repeated, now for the היכל. The ברייתא shows that the rule applies the same way at each place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pattern holds at every place. The חכמים say an interrupted unit is redone in full. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say only the missing sprinklings are done. Either way, nothing before this unit is repeated.

keyTerms.meaning: Some, or part of.
He does not begin except. In other words, he begins only.

steps.whatToRemember: Each place (לפני ולפנים, היכל, מזבח) is its own כפרה. A finished unit is never repeated. For an interrupted unit, the חכמים say restart that unit, and רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say continue from where he stopped.

phrases.english: If he gave some of the sprinklings in the Sanctuary
and the blood spilled,
he brings other blood
and begins from the start in the Sanctuary.
Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say:
He begins only from the place where he stopped.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָתַן מִקְצָת מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁבַּהֵיכָל וְנִשְׁפַּךְ הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the Step 13 dispute for the next place, the היכל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: restart the interrupted היכל unit. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון: continue from where he stopped.

steps.title: Blood spills after the היכל unit is finished
steps.stepSummary: If the כהן גדול finished the היכל sprinklings and then the blood spilled, he brings new blood and starts only the מזבח unit.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he finished the sprinklings in the היכל and then the blood spilled, he brings other blood and starts from the beginning of the sprinklings on the מזבח.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to the next stage of the service. The blood spilled after the היכל sprinklings were already completed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This follows the same pattern as Step 14. Each completed unit (לפני ולפנים, היכל, מזבח) counts as its own finished כפרה, so the היכל sprinklings are not repeated. He only starts the next unit, the מזבח, using new blood.

keyTerms.meaning: Sprinklings, or presentations, of blood
The blood spilled
From the beginning
The golden altar in the היכל. This is the 'מזבח' meant in this context

phrases.english: If he finished the sprinklings in the Sanctuary
and the blood spilled
he brings other blood
and begins at the start of the sprinklings on the altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּמַר מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁבַּהֵיכָל וְנִשְׁפַּךְ הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of cases, moving from the היכל unit to the מזבח unit
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A completed היכל unit is not repeated. New blood is used starting from the מזבח unit.

steps.title: Blood spills partway through the altar sprinklings
steps.stepSummary: If the blood spills partway through the מזבח sprinklings, the חכמים say to restart the מזבח unit. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say to continue from where he stopped.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he gave some of the sprinklings on the מזבח and the blood spilled, he brings other blood and starts from the beginning of the מזבח sprinklings. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say he begins from the place where he stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the same disagreement as in Steps 13 and 15, now applied to the third unit, the מזבח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For the חכמים, a unit that was started but not finished does not count, so the whole unit must be redone with the new blood. For רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, every sprinkling that was already done stays valid, so he simply picks up where he left off.

keyTerms.meaning: Some, or part of
From the place where he stopped
He begins

phrases.english: If he gave some of the sprinklings on the altar
and the blood spilled
he brings other blood
and begins at the start of the sprinklings on the altar.
Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say:
He begins from the place where he stopped.

steps.triggerLanguage: נָתַן מִקְצָת מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁבַּמִּזְבֵּחַ וְנִשְׁפַּךְ הַדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same מחלוקת from Steps 13 and 15 to the מזבח unit
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: restart the מזבח unit. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון: continue from where he stopped.

steps.title: Blood spills after all the sprinklings are done
steps.stepSummary: If all the מזבח sprinklings were finished and only the leftover blood spilled, everyone agrees that nothing is held back.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he finished the sprinklings on the מזבח and then the blood spilled, everyone agrees that it does not hold anything back.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last case: all the sprinklings are done, and only the leftover blood spilled. Here there is no disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leftover blood (שיריים) is supposed to be poured at the base of the outer altar. This pouring is a מצוה, but it is not required for the כפרה to work. So losing that blood does not mean bringing a new animal, according to all opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: Everyone agrees; all opinions
They do not hold back; they are not essential for the service to be valid
The leftover blood, poured at the base of the outer altar

steps.whatToRemember: There are three units: לפני ולפנים, היכל, and מזבח. A finished unit is never repeated. For an unfinished unit, the חכמים say to restart it, while רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say to continue from where he stopped. The leftover blood is not essential at all.

phrases.english: If he finished the sprinklings on the altar
and the blood spilled
everyone agrees that they (the leftovers) are not essential.

steps.triggerLanguage: גָּמַר מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁבַּמִּזְבֵּחַ וְנִשְׁפַּךְ הַדָּם דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל לָא מְעַכְּבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the series of cases with the one case where everyone agrees
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Losing the leftover blood after all the sprinklings are done does not hold back the כפרה.

steps.title: Both sides learn from the same verse
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that both sides of the מחלוקת learn their view from one verse: ״מִדַּם חַטַּאת הַכִּפּוּרִים אַחַת בַּשָּׁנָה״.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Both of them learned their view from one verse: 'From the blood of the חטאת of atonement, once a year.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next step. רבי יוחנן names the source verse, and the next step explains how each side reads it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement is not based on two different verses. It comes from two ways of reading the same word, 'אחת' (one), in this verse.

keyTerms.meaning: One verse
They expounded; they learned from
The sin-offering of atonement
Once a year

steps.confusionAlert: 'Both of them' refers to the unnamed חכמים, who are understood to be רבי מאיר, on one side, and רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון on the other side.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
And both of them expounded one verse:
"From the blood of the sin-offering of atonement
once a year"

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the rulings to the source in the verse behind them
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both opinions come from one verse in שמות, chapter 30, verse 10.

steps.title: One חטאת versus one sprinkling
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר reads 'אחת' as one animal (חטאת). רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון read it as one sprinkling (חטוי).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds: I told you one חטאת, and not two חטאות. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון hold: I told you one sprinkling, and not two sprinklings.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן explains how each side reads the word 'אחת' in the verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, one unit must be done entirely with the blood of one animal. So if the blood spills partway, the unit restarts with the new blood. For רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון, the verse only says each sprinkling is done once. So a sprinkling already done is not repeated, and he continues from where he stopped.

keyTerms.meaning: Holds; is of the opinion
Sin-offering, meaning the animal itself
A sprinkling, the act of applying the blood
I told you (the Torah speaking)

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the whole מחלוקת depends on whether the תורה requires one animal or one act. That is why the two sides disagree about continuing versus restarting.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
I told you one sin-offering,
and not two sin-offerings.
Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon hold:
I told you one sprinkling,
and not two sprinklings.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי מֵאִיר סָבַר חַטָּאת אַחַת אָמַרְתִּי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the two readings of the verse named in Step 19
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: one animal per unit. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון: each sprinkling once, so earlier sprinklings stay valid.

steps.title: רבי יעקב's distinction about the לוג of oil
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records רבי saying that רבי יעקב taught him a distinction regarding the לוגין of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי said: רבי יעקב made a distinction for me regarding the לוגין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new point with a ברייתא. This line sets up a discussion about the oil of the מצורע, where the rule may be different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: At first the גמרא reads 'חִלֵּק' as saying that רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון agree to the restart rule for the מצורע's לוג of oil. The next step challenges this reading, and Step 23 corrects it: רבי יעקב actually taught that the same מחלוקת applies to the oil.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא
רבי יהודה הנשיא
He made a distinction
Measures of oil (a לוג), here the oil used to purify a מצורע

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi said:
Rabbi Yaakov made a distinction for me regarding the lugin.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא אָמַר רַבִּי לִי חִלֵּק רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּלּוּגִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a case where the 'continue from where he stopped' view may not apply
steps.mimraCoreRuling: At first glance, the oil of the לוגין is distinguished from the blood. Steps 22-23 challenge this reading and correct it: the same מחלוקת applies to the oil.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows the same argument about the oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the earlier distinction about the לוגין with a ברייתא. In it, רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון argue about spilled oil exactly as they argue about spilled blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do they really not argue here? But a ברייתא teaches: if the כהן did some of the inside sprinklings of oil and the לוג spilled, he brings another לוג and starts the sprinklings in the היכל from the beginning. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say: he starts from where he stopped. If he finished the היכל sprinklings and the לוג spilled, he brings another לוג and starts from the beginning of the thumb placements. If he did some of the thumb placements and the לוג spilled, he brings another לוג and starts the thumb placements over. רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון say: he starts from where he stopped. If he finished the thumb placements and the לוג spilled, everyone agrees that the head placements do not hold anything back.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised by the earlier claim. It quotes a ברייתא showing that רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון do argue about the מצורע's לוג of oil.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier claim said the לוגין are treated differently from the blood. This ברייתא sets up the oil in the same units as the blood: the היכל sprinklings, then the thumb placements, then the head. Inside each unit there is the same מחלוקת of 'restart the unit' versus 'continue from where he stopped.' So the claimed difference seems to fall apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא? (opens a challenge from a ברייתא)
A measure of oil; here, the oil used to purify a מצורע
The seven sprinklings of oil toward the Holy of Holies, called 'of the היכל' because they are aimed toward it (the כהן stands in the עזרה)
The thumbs and big toes (with the ear) of the מצורע, where oil is placed
The remaining oil put on the מצורע's head
Hold back; are essential, so that the process fails without them

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two units with the blood of יום כפור. Here the topic is the oil of a מצורע: first the sprinklings in the היכל, then the placements on the thumbs and toes, and last the head. The structure matches the blood, but the subject is different.

phrases.english: And do they not [disagree]?
phrases.notes: An expression of surprise at the earlier claim about the לוגין

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא:
If he gave some of the inside presentations
phrases.notes: The sprinklings of oil done inside, in the היכל

phrases.english: and the log spilled
he brings another log
and starts from the beginning of the presentations in the Sanctuary.
Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say:
He begins from the place where he stopped.
If he finished the presentations in the Sanctuary
and the log spilled
he brings another log
and begins from the start of the presentations on the thumbs.
If he put some of the presentations on the thumbs
and the log spilled
he brings [another] log
and begins from the start of the presentations on the thumbs.
Rabbi Elazar and Rabbi Shimon say:
He begins from the place where he stopped.
If he finished the presentations on the thumbs
and the log spilled
everyone agrees
the presentations on the head are not indispensable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֹא? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי's statement in step 21 that the לוגין are different
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of רבי's statement in step 21 that רבי אלעזר and רבי שמעון agree the לוג of oil must be restarted (so they do not dispute it there)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly records the same 'restart versus continue' מחלוקת about the oil, so the claimed difference is contradicted

steps.title: Changing the wording: רבי יעקב taught the argument about the oil too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the wording of רבי's statement. It should read that רבי יעקב taught him this same מחלוקת regarding the לוגין.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: רבי יעקב taught me this [same argument] regarding the לוגין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by correcting the wording of רבי's statement. Now רבי's statement agrees with the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier reading had רבי treating the לוגין differently from the blood. The corrected reading says the opposite: רבי יעקב taught that the same מחלוקת also applies to the לוגין. With this change, the two sources fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: Say [instead]; used to correct or change the wording of a source
Taught
The logs of oil (plural of לוֹג)

phrases.english: Say [instead]:
phrases.notes: The גמרא corrects the wording of רבי's statement

phrases.english: Rabbi Ya'akov taught me [this dispute] regarding the lugin.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵימָא: לִי שָׁנָה רַבִּי יַעֲקֹב בַּלּוּגִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Correcting the wording of the source (אימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי's statement seemed to say the לוגין are different from the blood
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי's statement actually says the same מחלוקת applies to the לוגין, which matches the ברייתא
steps.whatToRemember: The 'restart the unit versus continue from where he stopped' מחלוקת applies both to the blood of יום כפור and to the oil of a מצורע.

steps.title: Why is the oil on the head not essential?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא's last line and asks for the reason that the head placements are not essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: the head placements do not hold anything back. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last line of the ברייתא and asks for its source. This sets up the next step, where it tries out an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agreed that if the לוג spilled after the thumb placements, nothing more is needed. The גמרא now wants to know why the head placement is optional, when the earlier placements are essential.

keyTerms.meaning: The Master said; quotes an earlier source in order to analyze it
What is the reason?

phrases.english: The Master said:
The presentations on the head are not indispensable.
What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר: מַתְּנוֹת הָרֹאשׁ — אֵין מְעַכְּבוֹת. מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic based on the last line of the ברייתא from step 22
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that the oil placed on the head is not essential

steps.title: Testing the source 'the rest of the oil' against the מנחה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the reason is the word 'והנותר' (the rest) in the verse. It rejects this, because the מנחה uses the same kind of word, and its leftovers are essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because it is written: 'And the rest of the oil' — then by that logic, look at 'And the rest of the מנחה.' Would you also say that it is not essential?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out an answer: the verse calls the head oil 'the rest,' so it is only leftover. It immediately attacks this answer using a similar verse about the מנחה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggestion is that the word 'the rest' makes something secondary and not essential. But the leftovers of the מנחה are also called 'the rest,' and the הלכה is that they are essential. If they are lost before the קמיצה is burned, a new one must be brought. So the word 'the rest' alone cannot prove that something is not essential.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; introduces a suggested answer that will be tested
'And the rest of the oil' (ויקרא י״ד:כ״ט)
But if so; introduces an unacceptable result of the suggestion
'And the rest of the מנחה' (ויקרא ב׳:ג׳)

steps.confusionAlert: The הלכה that the head oil is not essential is never in doubt. Only the proof from 'והנותר' is challenged here, and the next step saves that proof by showing the מצורע has two 'leftover' words.

phrases.english: If we say it is because it is written:
"And the rest of the oil"
phrases.notes: ויקרא י״ד:כ״ט, about the oil placed on the מצורע's head

phrases.english: But if that is so:
"And the rest of the meal-offering"
so too, would they not be indispensable?!
phrases.notes: No. The leftovers of the מנחה are essential.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דִּכְתִיב: וְהַנּוֹתָר מִן הַשֶּׁמֶן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Suggests an answer to the question in step 24 and immediately challenges it
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggested source 'והנותר מן השמן' as proof that the head oil is not essential
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word appears for the מנחה, and its leftovers are essential. So the word 'the rest' cannot by itself mean 'not essential.'
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a single word like 'the rest' is not enough on its own to prove a הלכה, because it must work the same way in other places in the תורה.

steps.title: The מצורע's oil uses two 'leftover' words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the oil of the מצורע is different from the מנחה. The תורה describes it with two 'leftover' expressions, 'ומיתר' and 'והנותר'. So the oil for the head is a leftover of a leftover and is not essential.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is different there, because it is written: 'And of the rest' and 'And the rest.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the last step. It explains why the מצורע's head oil is not essential even though the מנחה's leftovers are essential.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the מנחה, the תורה uses only one 'leftover' word, and those leftovers are essential. With the מצורע, the תורה says 'ומיתר' (and of the rest) for the ear, thumb, and toe, and then 'והנותר' (and the rest) for the head. That double wording shows the head gets only what is left over from the leftovers, so leaving it out does not ruin the service.

keyTerms.meaning: It is different there. This tells us the case being discussed has a special feature.
As it is written. This brings a verse as the source.
And of the rest. This is the first 'leftover' word, used for the ear, thumb, and toe (ויקרא יד:יז).
And the rest. This is the second 'leftover' word, used for the head (ויקרא יד:יח).

steps.whatToRemember: One 'leftover' word, as with the מנחה, does not make something non-essential. Two 'leftover' words, as with the מצורע's oil, make the head placement a 'leftover of a leftover', which is not essential.
steps.confusionAlert: The '...' inside the quote is not a missing piece of the גמרא's argument. It joins two separate verses. The point is that both words appear, 'ומיתר' in one verse and 'והנותר' in the next.

phrases.english: It is different there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the oil of the מצורע, as opposed to the מנחה.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And of the rest ... and the rest.'
phrases.notes: Two verses (ויקרא יד:יז-יח), giving two 'leftover' expressions in a row.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאנֵי הָתָם, דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 25 by pointing to the double 'leftover' wording that is unique to the מצורע.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the cases through verse wording: the מצורע has two 'leftover' words, while the מנחה has only one.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the מנחה's leftovers, called by a 'rest' word, are essential, the מצורע's head oil, also called 'the rest', should be essential too.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מצורע's head oil is a leftover of a leftover ('ומיתר' and then 'והנותר'), so it is not essential.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains the ברייתא's ruling that the head placement does not hold back the מצורע's purification.

steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled yet. This line just tells us that a new אמורא statement is starting, and it will be explained once its content appears.
